questions.prompt: A continuous random variable $X$ has a probability density function $f(x)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the value of $P(X = 4.5)$ and explain why $P(X \le 4.5) = P(X < 4.5)$ for any continuous random variable.

questions.prompt: A continuous random variable $Y$ follows the normal distribution $Y \sim \text{N}(80, 25)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the mean $\mu$ and calculate the standard deviation $\sigma$ of $Y$.

questions.prompt: The random variable $X$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu = 50$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 4$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the standard score $z$ corresponding to $x = 56$, and state whether $x$ lies above or below the mean.

questions.prompt: Let $Z \sim \text{N}(0, 1)$ denote the standard normal variable.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Using the standard normal cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$, find $P(Z > 0.8)$.

questions.prompt: The random variable $Z$ has the standard normal distribution $Z \sim \text{N}(0, 1)$.
A continuous random variable $W$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu = 35$ and standard deviation $\sigma = 8$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Without standardising, state the value of $P(W > 35)$ and justify your answer using a geometric property of the normal curve.

questions.prompt: The masses $X$ grams of apples harvested in an orchard are normally distributed with mean 150 g and standard deviation 16 g, so that $X \sim \text{N}(150, 16^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen apple has a mass less than 166 g.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen apple has a mass greater than 166 g.

questions.prompt: The heights $X$ cm of sunflowers in a commercial nursery are normally distributed with mean $180\text{ cm}$ and standard deviation $15\text{ cm}$, so that $X \sim \text{N}(180, 15^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen sunflower has a height less than $165\text{ cm}$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A random sample of 600 sunflowers is selected from the nursery. Find the expected number of sunflowers in the sample with a height between $165\text{ cm}$ and $180\text{ cm}$.

questions.prompt:
The recorded delivery times $T$ minutes for 104 packages are summarised in the following grouped frequency table:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Delivery time (minutes)} & 40 \le t < 50 & 50 \le t < 60 & 60 \le t < 70 & 70 \le t < 80 & 80 \le t < 90 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 6 & 22 & 48 & 23 & 5 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State two distinct features of the frequency distribution that suggest that a normal distribution could be a suitable model for the delivery times.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Assuming delivery times are modeled by $T \sim \text{N}(65, 8^2)$, calculate the probability that a randomly chosen delivery takes between 53 and 73 minutes.

questions.prompt: A commuter train is scheduled to depart at 08:30. A passenger arrives at the platform at time $X$, measured in minutes after 08:00, where $X \sim \text{N}(26, 2.5^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that the passenger arrives after the train departs (that is, arrives after 08:30).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: On a certain day, train departure is delayed until 08:32. Find the probability that the passenger arrives at the platform between 08:24 and 08:32.

questions.prompt: The continuous random variable $Y$ follows a normal distribution with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$, where $\mu = 4\sigma$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find $P(Y > 1.6\mu)$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find $P(Y < 0.7\mu)$.

questions.prompt:
A factory manufactures steel rods whose lengths $L\text{ cm}$ are normally distributed with mean $120\text{ cm}$ and standard deviation $2.5\text{ cm}$, so that $L \sim \text{N}(120, 2.5^2)$. Rods are classified into three categories according to their lengths:
- Short: $L < 116\text{ cm}$
- Standard: $116 \le L \le 124\text{ cm}$
- Long: $L > 124\text{ cm}$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the probability that a randomly chosen rod is classified as Long.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Show that the probability that a randomly chosen rod is classified as Standard is $0.8904$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Given that a randomly chosen rod is not Short, find the conditional probability that it is classified as Standard, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt:
A company manufactures ceramic tiles on two different production lines, Line A and Line B. The breaking strength $X$ (in megapascals, MPa) of tiles from each line follows a normal distribution:
- Line A: $X_A \sim \text{N}(44.0, 3.0^2)$
- Line B: $X_B \sim \text{N}(46.0, 3.2^2)$
A tile is designated as High Grade if its breaking strength exceeds $50.0\text{ MPa}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen tile produced by Line A is High Grade.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen tile produced by Line B is High Grade.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A storage crate contains a mixture of tiles consisting of $70\%$ from Line A and $30\%$ from Line B. A tile is chosen at random from the crate. Calculate the probability that the tile is High Grade, and hence, given that the chosen tile is High Grade, find the probability that it was produced by Line B.
